title: Pineapple and Coconut Gelato
changes_from_base: Reduced crushed pineapple and coconut milk replace the pistachio milk, with milk powder for body and a lighter 3-yolk custard; no cornflour.
summary: A tropical gelato of reduced pineapple and coconut milk, set with a light yolk custard and finished with toasted coconut.

ingredients.item: unsweetened desiccated coconut, toasted, to serve

steps.title: Reduce the pineapple
steps.text: Simmer the pineapple and its juice in a wide pan, stirring often, until almost no liquid is left, 15-20 min. Cool.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Heat half the coconut milk with the milk, sugar and milk powder, whisking out any lumps, until it steams.

steps.title: Yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks in the bowl, then slowly whisk in a ladle of the hot coconut milk and pour everything back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat until it thickens slightly and reaches 77-80 °C. Off the heat, stir in the rest of the coconut milk and the vanilla.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the custard with the cooked pineapple until nearly smooth; small flecks of fruit are fine. Cool over iced water, cover and chill overnight.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min until it mounds on a spoon.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container and freeze for at least 3 h. Scatter with toasted coconut to serve.

tips: Cooking the pineapple down concentrates its flavour and stops ice crystals forming.
Use full-fat coconut milk and shake the tin well before opening.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan for 2-3 min, watching closely, as it burns quickly.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10-15 min in the fridge before scooping.
